core: Both communities check the reliability of an automated grader/scorer by resubmitting the exact same completed answers to it more than once and comparing the resulting verdicts or numeric scores. Because the answer content itself is unchanged between submissions, any difference in the grader's output on the repeated pass reveals inconsistency or noise in the scoring process itself, rather than any real change in answer quality. This resubmission-and-compare method is used as evidence for how much the scorer's judgments can be trusted or vary across repeated evaluations of the same material.
quote_1: Reflowed line breaks, changed nothing else, resubmitted through the same grader. 9 out of 80 flipped verdicts.
quote_2: The same completed answers were then submitted to the scorer on four dates separated by at least 21 days.
